meta.title: Site Visit Checklist | Reno Stars
meta.description: Internal checklist for Reno Stars site visits. Pick the scope and capture everything the quote needs in one pass.

hero.title: Site Visit Checklist
hero.subtitle: Pick what the client wants. The page shows only the checks that scope needs — the same steps the quoting system will price.
hero.note: This page is for Reno Stars staff. Nothing you tick is sent anywhere; it stays on this phone until you clear it.

picker.modelHint: Match the client's intent. If unsure, pick the closest and note the difference.
picker.addonsHint: Tick what the client asked for. Each one adds its own checks below.
picker.empty: Pick a scope above to build the checklist.

items.label: Confirm the client's name and the full address you're standing at
items.hint: Street number and city become the project's PO number later — get it exactly right.

items.label: Best phone number and preferred language for the person who decides
items.hint: Not always the person who let you in.

items.label: Parking and material drop-off — where does a truck actually go?
items.hint: Lane access, permit zone, distance from the door. This is a real cost.

items.label: Strata or rental? Get the bylaws, work-hour limits and elevator booking rules
items.hint: Ask for the strata form now. It delays more jobs than anything else on this list.

items.label: Year the building was built
items.hint: Pre-1990 changes the whole quote — see hazards below.

items.label: Will anyone be living here during the work?
items.hint: Decides floor protection, dust walls, and whether we need to stage the work.

items.label: Locate and photograph the water shutoff
items.hint: Unit shutoff and building shutoff. Test that it actually turns.

items.label: Locate and photograph the electrical panel
items.hint: Note free breaker slots and whether it's fuses or breakers.

items.label: Wide photos of every wall in the work area, plus the ceiling and floor
items.hint: Stand in each corner. You will not get a second visit.

items.label: Photos of the path from the door to the work area
items.hint: Stairs, turns, narrow doorways — anything a vanity or slab has to fit through.

items.label: Overall room dimensions and ceiling height
items.hint: Length, width, height. Note bulkheads and any slope.

items.label: Client's target start date and any hard deadline
items.hint: Ask why, if there's a deadline. It's usually a move-in or a family event.

conditions.title: Site conditions
conditions.subtitle: Not line items on the quote, but they move the price more than anything else. Check all of them.

items.label: Pre-1990 building — flag asbestos testing
items.hint: WorkSafeBC requires a hazardous materials survey before demolition. Do not promise a price without it. Popcorn ceilings, vinyl floor tile, drywall mud and pipe wrap are the usual suspects.

items.label: Existing drain and supply piping — ABS, copper, PEX, cast iron, or galvanized
items.hint: Look under the sink and at any exposed basement runs. Cast iron or galvanized means the relocation cost is not standard.

items.label: Signs of active or past water damage
items.hint: Soft floor at the toilet or tub, staining on the ceiling below, musty smell, lifting tile. Photograph and note it in writing — this protects us both.

items.label: Visible mould
items.hint: Behind the toilet, at the tub surround, under the sink. Remediation is a separate scope.

items.label: Subfloor type and condition, and floor level
items.hint: Plywood or concrete slab. Check level with a 4ft level in two directions — an out-of-level floor means self-levelling before tile.

items.label: Any wall being opened or removed — is it load-bearing?
items.hint: If there's any doubt, it needs an engineer's letter. Note joist direction above.

items.label: Does this scope trigger a permit?
items.hint: Moving plumbing or gas, structural changes, new circuits, or changing the room's use. Confirm the municipality — Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond and Surrey all differ.

items.label: Popcorn ceiling present in or next to the work area
items.hint: Pre-1990 popcorn must be tested before it's touched. Even where we aren't removing it, note it — vibration cracks it.

items.label: Window inside the tub or shower area
items.hint: Needs a waterproofed return and usually a tempered replacement. Measure it and photograph the sill condition.

items.label: Where does the existing exhaust fan actually vent to?
items.hint: Roof, soffit, or straight into the attic. Venting into the attic is a defect we have to correct.

items.label: Access above the work area — attic, crawlspace, or a finished unit
items.hint: Decides whether potlights and relocated venting are straightforward or invasive.

items.label: Any gas appliance in or near the scope
items.hint: Gas work needs a licensed ticket and its own permit. Photograph the shutoff.

scope.title: Scope checks
scope.subtitle: Driven by the job type and add-ons you picked. Each card is a step the quote will contain.

captureLabels.brand: Brand, if the client already bought it

provides.title: Confirm who supplies what
provides.subtitle: These are install-only by default — the client buys them. Confirm each one out loud and write down what they've already bought.
provides.note: If the client wants us to supply any of these, mark it and get the model they want. It changes the quote.

demolition.label: Demolition
checks: List exactly what comes out and what stays — walk the room with the client and point at each item
Where does the debris go? Bin location, or how many trips to the truck
Check for a garburator, water softener, or anything plumbed in that isn't obvious
Note anything the client wants kept or salvaged

drywall.label: Drywall repair
checks: Wall condition behind the fixtures coming out — tile-over-tile, plaster, or standard board
Note any wall that isn't plumb or straight; it shows badly once new tile goes on
Check for insulation in exterior walls while you're guessing at what's behind them

popcornRemoval.label: Popcorn removal
checks: Confirm the pre-1990 asbestos test is flagged — do not price removal without it
Measure the ceiling area to be smoothed
Is the popcorn painted? Painted popcorn is slower and sometimes has to be boarded over instead

epv.label: Electrical, plumbing & venting
checks: Write down every single relocation the client wants, item by item, with the new position measured from a fixed wall
Photograph the existing rough-in positions before you leave
Confirm access below or behind — is the ceiling under this room finished?
Note the existing pipe material at every point you're relocating

bench.label: Shower bench
checks: Which wall, what length, and how deep
Confirm the bench doesn't land on the shower's only glass panel line
Check the wall behind can carry it — exterior wall means insulation loss

niche.label: Shower niche
checks: Position and size, measured from the finished floor and from the corner
Confirm the wall cavity is free — no vent stack, no plumbing, and check the other side of the wall
Metal edge or mitered tile edge? Ask the client and note the answer
LED strip inside the niche? That needs a power source nearby

ponywall.label: Ponywall
checks: Length and finished height
Is the glass panel landing on top of it? The glass supplier needs the finished height
Check what's underneath — the ponywall needs to sit on solid framing

encloseDoorOpening.label: Enclose door opening
checks: Opening width and height
Confirm it isn't load-bearing before you promise anything
What's the finish on both sides — matching two different wall finishes is extra
Flooring will need patching where the threshold was

newDoorOpening.label: New door opening
checks: Where exactly, measured from a fixed corner, and how wide
Load-bearing check — note joist direction above. If in doubt, engineer's letter
Anything in the wall: outlets, switches, plumbing, ducting
Confirm swing direction and whether a door is included

showerWall.label: Shower wall & waterproofing
checks: Measure each wall of the wet area, floor to ceiling
Note the ceiling height and whether tile runs to the ceiling or to a bulkhead
Check the existing wall for movement or rot behind the current surround
Photograph the corner where the two wet walls meet

floorTile.label: Floor tile
checks: Measure the floor area, and note the room's out-of-square if it's obvious
Has the client picked the tile? Size and finish change the labour
Existing floor build-up — how many layers are coming off, and what's the height difference at the doorway
Check the floor is level; note where it isn't

showerBase.label: Tiled shower base
checks: Measure the base footprint and the curb position
Confirm the drain location and whether it's moving
Floor build-up available for the slope — a tiled base needs height
Note the tile size the client wants on the base; small format is required on a sloped pan

tub.label: Tub
checks: Measure the alcove: length, width, and height to the top of the intended tile
Confirm the client's tub will fit through the door and down the hallway
Drain position — left, right, or centre — and whether it matches the new tub
Record the brand and model if they've already bought it

lvpFlooring.label: LVP flooring
checks: Measure the area, plus any closet or nook that carries through
Existing floor — is it coming out, or are we going over it?
Check level and note any dips; LVP telegraphs an uneven subfloor
Transition heights at every doorway

tubFaucet.label: Tub faucet
checks: Is the client supplying it? Record brand and model
Existing valve position and height — is it moving?
Confirm it's a tub-and-shower diverter or tub-only

showerDrain.label: Shower drain system
checks: Existing drain position and pipe material
Is the drain moving? Measure the new position from two walls
Access below to make the connection — what's under this floor?

tMouldings.label: T mouldings & reducers
checks: Count and measure every transition — doorways, and where two floor types meet
Note the height difference at each one
Match to the adjacent flooring the client is keeping

tubDrain.label: Tub drain
checks: Client-supplied? Record brand and finish so it matches the faucet
Existing drain and overflow position
Access below for the connection

tubShowerWall.label: Tub shower wall & waterproofing
checks: Measure all three alcove walls, floor to tile height
Confirm where the tile stops — ceiling, bulkhead, or a set height
Check the existing surround for water damage behind it
Note any window or niche inside the wet zone

cabinets.label: Kitchen cabinets
checks: Measure every wall run at counter height AND at upper-cabinet height — they differ
Mark every obstruction on the sketch: windows, doors, outlets, vents, radiators, bulkheads
Ceiling height at both ends of each run, and check it for level
Island: size, and confirm there's clearance all around it
Appliance sizes — fridge, stove, dishwasher, hood. Measure the existing openings
Confirm cabinet style and colour with the client, and whether it's prefab or custom

tile.label: Wall tile
checks: Measure each wall being tiled, floor to the finish height
Confirm the finish height: ceiling, bulkhead, or crown line
Tile size and layout the client wants — it changes the labour
Note edge treatment at every outside corner

quartzStep.label: Quartz curb step
checks: Curb length and width
Confirm the stone matches the countertop or what the client picked
Note whether the curb is standard height or being lowered

glassDoor.label: Shower glass door
checks: Measure the opening width and the intended finished height
Confirm hinge side and swing direction with the client
Is there a ponywall or bench the glass has to land on?
Standard prefab or custom? Custom needs a separate measure after tiling

underCabinetLed.label: Under-cabinet LED strip
checks: Total run length under the uppers
Where does the power come from, and is there a switch or is it always-on?
Confirm the client wants the driver hidden inside a cabinet

grabBars.label: Grab bars
checks: How many, and mark the exact position and height with the client present
Blocking must go in the wall before tile — confirm the positions are final
Client-supplied or ours? Record the finish

cornerShelves.label: Corner shelves
checks: How many and at what heights
Confirm they don't clash with the niche or the glass panel
Material and finish to match the tile

ledSwitch.label: LED strip switch
checks: Where does the switch go? Measure from the corner
Dimmable or standard — ask
Is there an existing gang box we can extend?

vanity.label: Vanity
checks: Measure the maximum width available, and the depth clear of the door swing and toilet
Plumbing rough-in: height off the floor and offset from the wall, for both drain and supply
Single or double sink — and confirm a double actually fits
Confirm style, colour, and door style with the client
Check the wall behind is flat; a bowed wall leaves a gap behind the vanity
Does the vanity fit through the bathroom door?

backsplash.label: Backsplash
checks: Measure the run length and the height from counter to uppers
Note every outlet and switch in the backsplash area
Confirm tile or quartz, and what happens behind the stove
Where does the backsplash stop at each end?

countertop.label: Countertop
checks: Measure every run: length and depth, including the island
Confirm the stone code the client picked
Sink type — undermount or drop-in — and whether the client has it on site for templating
Note edge profile, overhang, and any waterfall end
Count cutouts: sink, cooktop, outlets in the island

gfciVanity.label: GFCI outlet (vanity)
checks: Existing outlet position and height; is it already GFCI?
Is it moving with the new vanity? Measure the new position
Check the circuit it's on

sink.label: Kitchen sink
checks: Client-supplied? Record brand and model — the countertop cutout depends on it
Confirm the sink is on site before the countertop template
Single or double bowl, and the cabinet width below it
Garburator? Note it now

vanitySink.label: Vanity sink
checks: Client-supplied? Record brand and model
Undermount, drop-in, or integrated with the top
Confirm it matches the vanity width and the faucet hole count

faucet.label: Kitchen faucet
checks: Client-supplied? Record brand and model
Hole count needed in the counter — including a soap dispenser or filter tap
Check clearance to the window behind the sink if there is one

vanityFaucet.label: Vanity faucet
checks: Client-supplied? Record brand, model and finish
Single hole, 4" centreset, or 8" widespread — this must match the sink
Wall-mount? That changes the rough-in and must be decided now

showerFaucet.label: Shower faucet
checks: Client-supplied? Record brand and model — the valve body has to be on site before walls close
Confirm the valve height and position with the client, marked on the wall
Rain head, hand shower, or both? Each is a separate outlet
Thermostatic or pressure-balance

showerDrainFixture.label: Shower drain fixture
checks: Client-supplied? Record the finish so it matches the faucet
Point drain or linear — a linear drain changes the base slope and must be decided now

toilet.label: Toilet
checks: Measure the rough-in: centre of the flange to the finished wall behind. Usually 12", but check
Clearance each side and in front, to the vanity and the wall
Client-supplied? Record brand and model
Is the toilet moving? That's a drain relocation, not a swap

bidet.label: Bidet
checks: Client-supplied? Record brand and model
Is there a nearby outlet for an electric seat? Most need one
Confirm water supply connection point

gfciToilet.label: GFCI outlet (toilet area)
checks: Where exactly — measure the position and height
Which circuit will it come off, and is there capacity
Usually this is for a bidet seat; confirm that's why

gfciOutlets.label: GFCI outlets
checks: Count how many, and mark each position
Note which are in the backsplash and their heights
Check the existing circuits and panel capacity

replaceSwitches.label: Replace switches
checks: Count the switches and note what each one controls
Any of them going dimmable?
Confirm the finish and colour the client wants

pendantLight.label: Pendant light
checks: How many, and mark the positions over the island or counter
Is there an existing box, or is this new wiring?
Client-supplied? Record brand and model, and note the hanging height they want

pendantLightSwitch.label: Pendant light switch
checks: Switch position, measured from the corner
Dimmable or standard
Can it join an existing gang box?

islandOutlet.label: Island outlet
checks: Position on the island, and whether it's in the side panel or a pop-up in the counter
Feed route — the wire has to get to the island under the floor
Confirm with the client where they actually plug things in

baseboard.label: Baseboard
checks: Measure the total run
Match the profile and height to the rest of the house if it's continuing
Note any outside corners and how many

mirror.label: Mirror
checks: Client-supplied? Record size and model
Confirm the size fits between the vanity light and the backsplash
Framed, frameless, or a medicine cabinet — a cabinet needs a wall recess decision now

vanityLight.label: Vanity light
checks: Client-supplied? Record brand and model
Existing box position and height — is it centred on the new vanity?
If it's moving, measure the new position and confirm with the client

fullPaint.label: Kitchen paint
checks: Wall and ceiling area, and ceiling height
Colour code — get it from the client in writing
Note the current finish and whether it needs priming
Confirm what's excluded: doors, trim, inside cabinets

hardware.label: Bathroom hardware
checks: Client-supplied? Record the finish so it matches the faucet
Mark each position with the client: towel bar, ring, paper holder
Anything landing on tile needs its position confirmed before tiling

exhaustFan.label: Exhaust fan
checks: Where does the existing one vent to? Trace it if you can
Client-supplied? Record brand and model, and check the CFM suits the room size
Existing opening size versus the new unit
Is it moving? Note the duct run to the new position

potlights.label: Potlights
checks: How many, what size, and mark the layout with the client
Access above — attic, or a finished ceiling below another unit?
Note joists, ducting, and anything in the ceiling cavity
Which switch will control them, and dimmable?

newSwitch.label: New switch
checks: Position, measured from the door frame
What does it control, and is it dimmable?
Existing gang box nearby to extend from?

baseboardReinstall.label: Reinstall baseboards
checks: Confirm the existing baseboard will survive removal — MDF usually doesn't
Measure the total run
Note the condition and whether it needs repainting after

baseboardNew.label: New MDF baseboard
checks: Measure the total run
Confirm the profile and height match the rest of the house
Count the outside corners

paint.label: Paint
checks: Wall and ceiling area, and ceiling height
Colour code in writing from the client
Current finish and whether primer is needed
Confirm what's excluded

touchUpPaint.label: Touch-up paint
checks: Ceiling height and roughly how much area needs touching up
Get the existing colour code — check the can in the garage or the closet
Warn the client that touch-up rarely blends perfectly on an aged wall

summary.title: Send it back to the office
summary.resetConfirm: Clear every tick and note on this checklist?
summary.shareTitle: Send this exact checklist to someone
summary.shareHint: Copies a link with this scope already selected.

names.bathroom-keep-tub: Keep existing tub (keeps tub faucet + drain too)
names.bathroom-keep-vanity: Keep existing vanity cabinet (countertop/sink/faucet not included)
names.bathroom-open-shower: Open shower (no glass door, no curtain)
